method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING, with a NOTHING-kind tag, where it does not answer); the dates in one module, Part II (the focus, survival) in another, Parts IV to X in a third, and a cases file for each; one regulative rule (taking proceedings in tort against a dead wrongdoer's estate within 12 months after the grant, s 7(1)(b)) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seats: the executor or administrator of a person who has died, bringing or continuing that person's claim for the estate, and a person with a claim against someone who has died (lrnt-survival.l4)

the person bringing a claim -- the injured person, a dependant, a person who suffers loss through the injured person, a worker, a family member in shock, a property owner, a person hurt by a dog, a blind or deaf person with an assistance dog -- and, where the Act addresses them, the employee who committed a tort at work (s 22A) and the person who killed or injured a dog (ss 33, 34) (lrnt-claims.l4)

scope: Part II whole (ss 5-9: survival, damages for the estate with the dust-disease rule, conditions for proceedings against an estate, s 8, s 9(1)); s 11(b), s 12(2), (3); ss 15, 16, 17(2), 18, 21, 21A; ss 22, 22A; ss 23-25; ss 26(1), (2), 27, 28; s 29A; ss 31-35. Out: ss 1, 3, 4 (machinery); s 9 savings; s 12(4), (5), ss 13, 14, 17(1), 19 (contribution between wrongdoers); s 20 (jury procedure); the pre-2001 s 16 under s 21A(3) (not deposited); s 26(3) (ranking among claimants); s 29 (saving).
